title: Global Resources Outlook 2024
book_use: Front matter; Chapters 1, 17, 18, 21, 23, and 27: global natural-resource extraction roughly tripled over the prior five decades and could rise another 60% from 2020 levels by 2060 without major change; use with the report's distributional inequality context, not as a universal anti-consumption claim.

title: Sustainable Materials Management: Non-Hazardous Materials and Waste Management Hierarchy
book_use: Chapters 1, 3, 10, 20, 22, and 27: source reduction and reuse rank above recycling/composting, followed by energy recovery, treatment, and disposal; grounds the ordering of questions without implying higher options always win lifecycle comparisons.

title: Recycling Basics and Benefits
book_use: Chapters 1 and 27: EPA encourages reduction and reuse before recycling and defines recycling within a larger materials-management hierarchy.

title: Global Waste Management Outlook 2024
book_use: Chapters 1, 22, and 27: municipal solid waste estimated at about 2.1 billion tonnes in 2023 and projected to about 3.8 billion tonnes by 2050 under prevailing trajectories; supports the argument that downstream processing alone cannot solve throughput growth.

title: Construction and Demolition Debris: Material-Specific Data
book_use: Chapter 5: U.S. construction and demolition debris generation estimated at about 600 million tons in 2018, more than twice municipal solid waste; demonstrates the scale of high-mass built stocks.

title: Sustainable Management of Construction and Demolition Materials
book_use: Chapters 5 and 6: preserving existing buildings, designing for adaptability, and optimizing components for disassembly and reuse are recognized C&D management strategies.

title: Material efficiency in clean energy transitions
book_use: Chapters 2, 5, 17, and 21: lifetime extension, renovation, steel reuse, material-efficient design and other strategies can reduce primary material demand in clean-energy transitions; use as systems evidence rather than a current policy forecast.

author_or_institution: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
title: Global Plastics Outlook: Economic Drivers, Environmental Impacts and Policy Options
book_use: Chapter 9: global plastics production estimated at 460 Mt and plastic waste at 353 Mt in 2019, with 9% ultimately recycled after losses; illustrates the gap between nominal recyclability and realized circulation.

title: Turning off the Tap: How the world can end plastic pollution and create a circular economy
book_use: Chapter 9: combines reduction of problematic/unnecessary plastic uses, redesign, reuse, and recycling; supports upstream intervention rather than recycling-only framing.

title: The Global E-waste Monitor 2024
book_use: Chapter 8: 62 billion kg of e-waste generated in 2022 and 22.3% documented as formally collected and recycled; supports the global e-waste scale and formal-recovery gap.

title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 establishing a framework for the setting of ecodesign requirements for sustainable products
book_use: Chapters 4, 14, 25, 26, and 27: framework can address durability, reusability, upgradability, reparability, remanufacturing, recycling, resource efficiency and Digital Product Passports for product groups brought under delegated requirements.

title: Digital Product Passport (DPP) — harmonised standards
book_use: Chapters 14, 25, and 26: current 2026 standardization work on identifiers, data carriers, access, interoperability and exchange for the ESPR Digital Product Passport infrastructure; use as current implementation evidence.

title: Sustainable products to be the norm for consumers as new regulation enters into force
book_use: Chapters 4 and 14: official summary of ESPR coverage including durability, reusability, upgradability, reparability, remanufacturing, recycling and product information.

title: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 concerning batteries and waste batteries
book_use: Chapters 7, 14, 17, 26, and 27: battery passport applicability from 18 February 2027 for specified EV, LMT, and larger industrial batteries, with model/individual information and differentiated access relevant to repair, remanufacturing, repurposing and recycling.

title: Circular economy: Council gives final approval to right-to-repair directive
book_use: Chapters 4 and 24: EU adoption of common repair rules in 2024; use for the legal direction toward repair services, parts/tools/information under covered categories and applicable requirements.

title: Right to repair products
book_use: Chapters 4 and 24: directive entered into force 30 July 2024 with Member State transposition due by 31 July 2026; use for current implementation timing, not to imply identical coverage across all products.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: Circular Economy Manufacturing Models
book_use: Chapters 2, 3, 12, 14, 25, and 26: distinguishes reuse, repair/remanufacturing, recycling and related manufacturing activities; grounds the book's treatment of circularity as a set of different state transitions rather than one loop.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: Reuse — Circular Economy Manufacturing Models
book_use: Chapters 2 and 12: inspection/testing and qualification are central to reuse routing; supports the claim that high-value circularity is information and assurance intensive.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: Remanufacture — Circular Economy Manufacturing Models
book_use: Chapters 12 and 15: remanufacturing can involve inspection, cleaning, refurbishment/replacement, reassembly and testing to return a product to a defined state.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: An information model for disassembly for reuse, recycling, and remanufacturing
book_use: Chapters 4, 12, 14, 25, and 26: early formal evidence that afterlife information and disassembly knowledge are manufacturing-system inputs.

title: Recycling of Critical Minerals — Executive summary
book_use: Chapters 7 and 17: long-run recycled supply can make significant contributions to lithium, nickel, cobalt, copper and other demand if collection and recovery improve; preserve the report's timing constraint that growing stocks still require primary supply.

title: Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 — Executive summary
book_use: Chapter 17: current 2026 project and demand scenarios continue to identify potential deficits and concentration risks for key minerals including copper and lithium; treat as scenario evidence, not certainty.

title: Extended Battery Producer Responsibility (EPR) Framework
book_use: Chapters 4, 9, 13, 20, and 26: producer responsibility can extend financial and/or physical responsibility into post-consumer stages; supports the design-feedback argument while preserving that EPR design varies by program.

title: Federal Acquisition Regulation Part 11 — Describing Agency Needs
book_use: Chapters 12, 15, and 16: current definitions distinguish reconditioned and remanufactured supplies; supports performance-category procurement rather than treating all non-new goods as undifferentiated used goods.

title: Federal Acquisition Regulation Subpart 52.2 — Text of Provisions and Clauses
book_use: Chapters 12 and 16: applicable clauses can allow offers of new, reconditioned, or remanufactured supplies under specified solicitation conditions; do not generalize to every federal procurement.

title: Water Reuse
book_use: Chapter 11: EPA defines water reuse as reclaiming water from varied sources, treating it, and reusing it for beneficial purposes; supports fit-for-purpose framing.

title: Water Reuse Action Plan 2.0
book_use: Chapter 11: EPA launched Water Reuse Action Plan 2.0 on 16 April 2026; use for current U.S. reuse-policy context, not as evidence that every reuse pathway is environmentally superior.

title: Wasted Food Scale
book_use: Chapter 10: prevention, donation and upcycling rank above lower pathways such as composting, anaerobic digestion, sewer disposal, incineration and landfill; supports the higher-use principle for food.

title: Food Waste Index Report 2024
book_use: Chapter 10: global food-waste measurement framework and 2022 estimates; use with UNEP's published methodological boundaries.

title: World squanders over 1 billion meals a day — UN report
book_use: Chapter 10: summarizes the 2022 estimate of 1.05 billion tonnes of food waste at household, food-service and retail levels, roughly one-fifth of food available to consumers.
